intro: Fully funded salaried PhD position at Umeå University on machine learning for graph transformations: interpretable, verifiable models combining deep learning with grammatical inference. No tuition.
description:
Overview

Umeå University’s Department of Computing Science offers a four-year PhD position focused on machine learning for graph transformations. The project explores a hybrid approach combining deep learning with grammatical inference to build models that are interpretable, efficient and mathematically verifiable, while retaining the flexibility of neural methods.

The position is a salaried doctoral employment under Swedish terms, with no tuition. It is mainly devoted to PhD research (at least 80% of the time) and may include up to 20% departmental service, usually teaching, which extends the total period to a maximum of five years.

Project Description

Graphs represent structured information from sentences and computer programs to social networks, and are becoming increasingly important as generative AI moves beyond text. This project learns transparent, rule-based rewriting systems that can transform graphs, check the correctness of AI-generated structures and guide neural networks during inference.

  • Combine grammatical inference, reinforcement learning and efficient search algorithms to discover rules and probabilities for modelling complex graph behaviour.
  • Develop interpretable and verifiable alternatives to opaque, heavy machine-learning models.
  • Potential applications include automated theorem proving, knowledge-graph inference and causal analysis.
  • Publish research outputs in theoretical computer science and symbolic machine learning.

Eligibility

  • A second-cycle degree, or completed course requirements of at least 240 ECTS credits including at least 60 ECTS at second-cycle level, or an equivalent foreign education/qualification.
  • At least 90 higher-education credits in computer science or a subject directly relevant to the specialisation.
  • Solid analytical and mathematical abilities, experience with machine learning, and experience with formal language or automata theory.
  • Strong English communication skills; the application must be written in English or Swedish. No formal English-test score is stated in the posting.
  • Meritorious: academic writing, strong Python programming, familiarity with knowledge graphs and graph neural networks.

How to Apply

  • Prepare a cover letter describing your research interests and reasons for applying, a CV, reprints/copies of BSc or MSc theses and relevant publications, degree certificates with courses and grades, and descriptions of other relevant experience.
  • Write the application in English or Swedish and attach documents in PDF format.
  • Submit electronically through Umeå University’s e-recruitment system so it is received no later than 30 November 2026.
  • Contact Professor Johanna Björklund for additional information about the project.
